fix: Read CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (keep the old name as a fallback), refuse or warn when no session id resolves rather than using 'none', and hash toplevel() instead of cwd.
text: Outside herdr the session id is read from $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, which Claude Code does not export (it exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; confirmed in this pane's env). Every Claude lane outside herdr in the same cwd gets agent 'session-none', so two lanes share one identity and one outbox, and check-reply cannot tell one lane's reply from the other's — the 'other lane' refusal the spec requires. The workspace also hashes os.getcwd() rather than the repo toplevel, so the same lane running check-reply from a subdirectory refuses its own reply.

fix: Re-read state after the POST and set only `sent` (write `sent` to a separate marker file, as events already do with .sent).
text: try_send reads the state file before the POST, which can take up to 3 s, and afterwards writes the whole state back with sent=True. A concurrent lane `close` or `stale` landing in that window gets overwritten with status 'open', which resurrects the packet, and check-reply then accepts a reply to a closed or stale packet. The driver flushes lane outboxes by design, so the two processes do share these files.

fix: With no floor hit, keep the claim (computed = one-way if hits else claim), or skip classification for info packets.
text: `new --door info --range R` on a range with no floor hits is refused. door.classify returns 'two-way' as its baseline (door.py:160), which outranks the 'info' claim, so packet.py promotes the door to two-way. A two-way packet requires a recommended option, so a valid info packet is rejected with exit 1. Reproduced in a scratch repo.

fix: Compile with re.DOTALL (or use [^\0]* instead of .*).
text: Globs compile without re.DOTALL, so the `.*` in `(?:/.*)?$` and `/.*$` stops at a newline. A floor path whose name contains a newline (e.g. `migrations/a\nb.sql`, which git allows and -z passes through) matches no rule and classifies as two-way. The red-team specialist confirmed this in a scratch repo. That breaks the fail-closed guarantee, though it is exotic for non-adversarial lanes.

fix: Use a hard wall-clock deadline, for example a worker thread with join(3) or resolving the host under a timeout, and install an opener that refuses redirects.
text: urlopen(timeout=3) bounds each socket operation, not the call: DNS resolution (MagicDNS down) and a slow-drip server can hold `new`/`close`/`event` well past the 3 s the scope promises. urllib also follows a 301/302 on a POST as a body-less GET; a 200 from that GET counts as sent, so the packet is marked sent but was never stored, e.g. an http:// URL that tailscale serve redirects to https.

fix: Catch OSError/ValueError per item in flush (report and skip), and around the two file reads.
text: flush → try_send reads `<pid>.json` (line 206) with no exception handling. A state file whose packet file is missing or corrupt crashes flush with a traceback and exit 1, and every later packet in the outbox stays unflushed. That contradicts 'harness errors never stop'. `--body-file` (line 264) and `check-reply --file` (line 375) also traceback on an unreadable file instead of the documented exit-1 refusal.

fix: Either have check-reply compare HEAD against head_sha for one-way packets (fail closed), or correct the docstring and have the caller run `stale` before applying a reply.
text: The docstring justifies stale's fail-open with 'applying a reply is gated by check-reply anyway'. check-reply checks only the recorded status and never compares HEAD with head_sha. A packet whose head moved but was never marked stale passes check-reply: the git-unreadable case this sentence covers, or any lane that never calls `stale`.

fix: Floor a path only via the repo file (e.g. `src/billing/` plus `!src/billing/`) and assert one-way.
text: test_negation_line_is_ignored is tautological. `db/migrations/` is already on the defaults floor, so the result is one-way whether or not `!` lines are honoured, and a regression that made negation work would stay green.

fix: Assert state['sent'] is True and 'Blocked' is not in stdout after the re-send; in the flush tests, assert s.posts and the state files.
text: The idempotent-retry test asserts the stub's own dedupe (len(s.posts)==1, where the stub drops 409s). It never asserts that the client treated the 409 as sent: state.sent true, no Blocked note. The flush tests at :173-184 likewise check printed counts but never s.posts or state.

fix: Map each invalid fixture to an expected error substring, and add ui and merged/stale fixtures.

fix: Decide in 1.5: default --range to the unit's base..HEAD, or refuse a two-way packet without --range when the lane has commits.

fix: Pass --ignore-submodules=none (and -c diff.ignoreSubmodules=none).
text: git diff honours diff.ignoreSubmodules and .gitmodules ignore=all, so a submodule pointer bump at a floor path can drop out of the name-status list and classify as two-way.

fix: Translate a leading '!' inside brackets to '^'.
text: The gitignore class `[!x]` (negated) is copied verbatim as the regex class `[!x]`, which matches '!' or 'x', the opposite of the author's intent, so a repo `.one-way-doors` line using it under-matches (fail-open). No default uses brackets.

fix: Use re.fullmatch-safe translation: replace a trailing unescaped `$` with `\Z`, or check with re.search(pattern.replace('$','\Z')).

ECMA-262 regex used by standard JSON Schema validators does not, so the queue service's validator may disagree. find_packet's fullmatch then makes such a packet unreachable.

fix: Raise SchemaError when additionalProperties is present and is not False.
